## 債市主線

科技股跌勢加劇，帶動避險需求並降低市場對聯準會進一步升息的預期，美國公債延續漲勢。2年期殖利率下降11.86個基點至4.4623%，降幅大於10年期的5.32個基點，後者收在4.8347%。前一交易日債市受惠於油價下跌，週四則在原油反彈之際續漲，因為市場對人工智慧建設背後融資安排與成長假設的疑慮，已從股票蔓延至公司債。

Nasdaq 100下跌6.36%，半導體股重挫12.25%。CoreWeave債券殖利率突破17%，SpaceX債務的違約保障成本創下新高；美國高收益債利差明顯擴大，強勢貨幣計價新興市場債利差則小幅走闊。不過，投資人並未全面撤離科技信用市場。Apple仍成功募得$75億，市場將其以股東回饋為優先的資金配置，與其他科技借款人龐大的基礎建設需求區分看待。

經濟數據與官員談話呈現不同訊號。美國首次申領失業救濟人數降至18.9萬人，低於預期；生產力增強，也使季度單位勞動成本意外下降。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack仍主張收緊政策，里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Tom Barkin則支持逐步升息。海外方面，英國央行升息至4%，並警告通膨將逼近5%；墨西哥卻意外降息至6.25%。這波美債上漲反映金融市場信心急遽調整，各國則持續面臨不同的通膨問題。

## 避險買盤壓過油價反彈與就業韌性

美股開盤後，美債行情出現轉折。原先殖利率隨油價自近期低點回升而走高，之後科技股跌勢加深，資金轉進公債。Capital Group固定收益投資總監Anmol Sinha認為，晶片股下跌讓市場擔心資本支出將放慢。市場除了尋求避險，也擔心AI基礎建設投資若減少，可能使經濟成長與政策利率預期下修；這兩項預期正是入秋稍早推升殖利率的因素。

收盤以短天期美債領漲。5年期殖利率下降8.14個基點至4.6045%，30年期僅降2.23個基點至5.2539%。2年與10年期利差擴大6.54個基點至37.24個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大9.63個基點至79.16個基點。漲勢集中在短端，顯示政策預期調整是較重要的推力。

10年期殖利率當日降幅主要來自實質殖利率。相應的抗通膨公債（TIPS）殖利率下降4.17個基點至2.5977%，10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1.15個基點至2.237%。本週累計的結構卻不同：名目殖利率下跌10.22個基點，損益兩平通膨率下跌11.28個基點，實質殖利率反而上升1.06個基點。週四實質殖利率顯著下行，但本週美債漲勢仍以通膨補償下降為主。過去一個月，10年期殖利率累計下降47.21個基點，其中實質部分下降34.63個基點。

利率衍生品反映情緒轉變，市場仍認為可能再度升息。據Bloomberg盤中報導，交易員仍較傾向預期聯準會於12月9日升息25個基點，但短期利率選擇權已出現押注按兵不動的交易，對明年進一步緊縮的押注也減少。美債選擇權同樣出現看漲需求：一筆交易押注10年期殖利率於下週底降至4.7%，另一筆11月20日到期的交易則瞄準約4.35%。這些部位表達的是可能情境，並非市場一致預測。

股市跌幅大，而且集中在令債權人不安的投資主題。S&P 500下跌4.36%至7,353.73點，Nasdaq 100收在26,629.81點；VIX跳升69.66%至28.18。Qualcomm與Arm的展望不如預期，增添個別公司壓力；民主黨在期中選舉勝出後，市場也擔心資料中心監管可能趨嚴。半導體指數經當日重挫後，本週累計下跌21.77%，過去一個月下跌31.59%。

油價反彈之際，美債仍受避險買盤支撐。Brent期貨上漲4.89%至每桶$99.25，WTI上漲3.50%至$91.20，但兩者仍較一週前低逾10%。黃金期貨上漲0.61%至每盎司$4,097.90，美元指數微升0.07%至101.584。當日資金撤出對經濟成長敏感的資產，油價則從近期跌勢中回升。

美國最新就業數據幾乎未顯示裁員加速。截至10月31日當週，首次申領失業救濟人數減少6,000人至18.9萬人，低於市場預估的19.6萬人。前週由19.4萬人上修至19.5萬人；四週移動平均減少2,250人至19萬4,750人。Reuters指出，當週人數追平7月低點，也是1969年以來最低。

持續申領數據則較弱。截至10月24日當週，持續申領人數增加2.3萬人至171.8萬人，高於預估的171萬人，前值則下修至169.5萬人。受保失業率維持1.1%。也就是說，新進失業人數偏低的同時，持續領取救濟的人數小幅增加。Challenger另行統計的10月企業宣布裁員人數為43,994人，前值43,281人，市場原估51,000人。

生產力提高，更直接帶動單位勞動成本改善。第3季非農企業生產力初值經季節調整後年化成長3.6%，高於預估的2.8%；產出增加3.7%，工時僅增0.1%。每小時報酬增加2.9%，但單位勞動成本反而下降0.7%，而非市場預期的上升0.6%。與去年同期相比，生產力成長2.1%，單位勞動成本則仍上升2.4%。

各生產部門的改善並不一致。製造業生產力年化僅增0.3%，產出增加1.3%，工時增加1%；耐久財生產力增加2.2%，非耐久財卻下降1.7%。製造業單位勞動成本年化上升2.7%，年增4%。整體每單位產出的勞動成本下降之際，工廠端仍承受成本壓力。

修正值也改變了比較基礎。第2季非農企業生產力成長率上修0.7個百分點至2.1%，單位勞動成本成長率同樣上修0.7個百分點至1.9%。2025年與2024年平均生產力成長率分別修正為2.3%與3.2%，均較原估高0.2個百分點。自2019年第4季以來，生產力年化成長2.2%，高於前一景氣循環的1.5%。勞動報酬占產出比率降至53%，創1947年開始統計以來最低。

Hammack對政策的看法仍偏緊。她在蘇黎世表示，政策須進入限制性立場，才能及時將通膨帶回2%；她偏好在可行情況下更頻繁地小幅調整，以降低政策落後情勢的風險。上週聯準會決定維持利率時，她是兩名異議者之一。她認為價格壓力廣泛，供給與需求因素皆有影響；長期呈現低招聘、低裁員的勞動市場，也出現可能轉強的些微跡象。

Barkin另行發言時重申支持逐步升息，但不願明言利率應升至何處。市場因股市引發的成長風險而調整預期，步伐因而快於這些官員公開立場的變化。

FHN Financial的Will Compernolle提醒，AI投資若逆轉，初期對就業的影響可能有限，因為這波熱潮屬資本密集型，新增職位相對不多；更廣泛的金融衝擊傳入經濟還需要時間。這有助於解釋，為何週度申領失業救濟人數仍異常低，週四金融市場卻大幅重估價格。

## AI信用風險重估，Apple順利取得資金

公司信用惡化最明顯的，是與AI建設週期密切相關的借款人。CoreWeave債券殖利率突破17%，較前一交易日進一步惡化；SpaceX違約保障成本創新高，增幅遠大於其他超大規模雲端業者。隨科技股賣壓擴散，投資人重新評估許可延宕、政治審視與資金需求的風險。

產業內部仍有重要差異。Bloomberg指出，其他超大規模雲端業者的債務保障成本僅小幅上升。其信用分析師Robert Schiffman認為，許可審查趨嚴、電網成本規範與地方反對聲浪若拖慢建設，降低資本密集程度及外部融資需求，反而可能有利大型科技客戶的信用。仰賴快速擴張的開發商則面臨更大壓力。Intrepid Capital Management的Hunter Hayes警告，部分債權人仰賴下一位貸款人提供還款資金，一旦取得融資的能力下降，公司可能無法完成計畫。

SpaceX的融資說明了這類風險的規模與複雜性。據知情人士透露，Goldman Sachs與Apollo正與投資人洽談，分銷上週簽訂、用於購買晶片的一筆約$400億設備融資租賃。在正式聯貸前，兩家公司已詢問潛在買家是否願意承接最高$5億的部分份額。這項安排的結構設計，是將債務置於SpaceX資產負債表之外。信用保障價格攀升之際，分銷洽談仍在進行。

另一項出售程序涉及約$5億資料中心貸款，其中一筆$2,500萬份額支持新墨西哥州的一處基地，屬於OpenAI、SoftBank與Oracle參與的Stargate計畫。RBC Global Asset Management的Andrzej Skiba表示，避險基金近幾週大量賣出AI相關債務，並解除槓桿部位；媒體與電信債務也出現賣壓。

各項專案的進展，為市場原有的政治疑慮增添具體的不確定性。據一名知情人士透露，Microsoft決定不續簽Nscale位於德州一座資料中心的合約，時間點在這家新創公司計畫上市之前。Oracle擬建、規模$1,650億的新墨西哥州園區也可能再度延宕，因其電力開發商同意給監管機關更多時間審查空污許可。另據知情人士透露，Micron因曠日持久的勞資爭議，暫停在台灣興建記憶體晶片廠的計畫。這些合約、監管及營運問題各不相同，卻都影響基礎建設交付時程。

Apple已完成的融資顯示，投資人仍依科技公司的商業模式加以區分。即使整體市場走弱，其分七批發行的$75億債券仍吸引約$310億高峰訂單，逾發行額四倍，天期從2年至10年。最長的2036年到期債，行銷過程中利差收窄25個基點，最終以較美債高55個基點定價。

相較之下，近期Microsoft發行的相近天期債券利差為65個基點，Meta為160個基點，Oracle為310個基點。Apple獲S&P Global Ratings評為AA+，資金預計用於一般公司用途，包括買回股票。Schiffman認為，Apple重返市場更偏向把握機會，而非迫於資金需求；相對於同業面臨的基礎建設支出，對股東分配資金仍是其更優先的資本配置。承銷行包括Bank of America、Deutsche Bank、Goldman Sachs與JPMorgan。

歐洲市場也顯示需求具選擇性。Meta新發行、總額€90億的六批債券，定價略低於面額，但首日交易的指示價格全部高於面額，連買方報價也在面額之上。最新報導的最終訂單簿為€620億，高於先前報導的€530億。Alphabet週一發行的歐元債，指示價格同樣高於面額。這些次級市場漲勢出現在新債提供可觀發行溢酬之後，與高槓桿AI借款人的價格顯著轉弱同時存在。

整體信用債報酬則反映美債殖利率下降與風險偏好走弱的拉鋸。含配息計算，LQD報酬約0.15%，HYG下跌0.31%，JNK下跌0.27%，EMB下跌0.52%。美國高收益債利差明顯擴大、強勢貨幣計價新興市場債利差小幅擴大，與公債強勁上漲形成對比。

科技業以外，Volkswagen雖為混合資本債融資付出高成本，仍吸引大量訂單。這筆€19.5億綠色債券分為兩批次順位債，殖利率分別為7.1%與7.45%，約比其流通在外的優先債高250個基點。Bloomberg對照歐洲ICE指數指出，優先與次順位債的利差約67個基點。兩批新債各自的訂單均逾發行額八倍。

募集資金將部分用於再融資2027年可贖回的混合資本債。新券票息為6.875%與7.25%，既有債券則為3.875%與3.748%。再融資成本升高之際，Volkswagen也面臨中國需求疲弱、關稅與競爭壓力，並因資產減記與重整費用而錄得第3季€58.6億營業虧損。信評機構給予混合資本債部分權益認列，因此即使成本較優先債高出許多，公司仍有維持這類工具以管理資產負債表的理由。Edmond de Rothschild投資組合經理Marc Lacraz提及Volkswagen的現金部位，並將逾7%的殖利率，與歐元BB級指數約5.5%的殖利率相比。

併購融資案源也持續推進。據知情人士透露，Goldman Sachs、Bank of America與Barclays獲選主導CD&R及McKesson收購Option Care Health所需的$31億融資，預計結合槓桿貸款、擔保債及無擔保債。出售時程仍待敲定，收購預計2027年上半年完成。這筆企業價值約$58億的交易完成後，CD&R將持有51%，McKesson在投入約$14億後持有49%。這批潛在供給出現之前，美國10月非投資等級債發行額為$146億，年減18%，槓桿貸款發行額則減少逾10%。

Bank of America另將信用總體、固定收益ETF及高評級債券交易業務整合為單一平台，由Rory O'Donovan與Amit Patel在原有職責之外共同領導。據Crisil Coalition Greenwich統計，截至10月，美國高評級與非投資等級債券日均交易額創下$616億紀錄，2025年為$552億。電子交易占美國高評級債交易的46%，高於去年的44%及2021年的30%。銀行表示，新架構將整合各項信用風險交易與避險工具的流動性供給。

## 英國升息凸顯通膨風險分歧

英國央行升息25個基點至4%，為2023年以來首次升息，全體決策委員都支持收緊政策。其中八人支持升息25個基點，Catherine Mann主張50個基點。因此，8比1指的是升息幅度的表決，並無委員支持維持利率不變。

總裁Andrew Bailey認為，可能有理由再升息一次，之後則更視條件而定。如果伊朗衝突的解決沒有進展，也沒有其他能減輕通膨壓力的消息，就可能需要再度調整；但他不認為週四必然是漫長升息循環的開端。決策公布後，交易員將12月升息機率推至約50%，並預期明年底前還會有近三次25個基點的升息。Bloomberg的決策報導指出，2年期英國公債殖利率上升約3個基點至4.77%；其整體市場報導則稱，10年期大致持平於5.13%。

新的通膨預測顯示，英國仍面臨顯著的物價壓力。央行預估CPI將於2027年第2季達到4.9%高峰，7月原估高點僅3.2%。明年1月管制價格上限重設時，家庭能源帳單預計增加約25%。這次預測採用截至10月27日的15天市場價格假設，Brent較7月預測高38%，天然氣高81%。Bailey表示，即使委員會事先知道過去48小時的能源價格變化，決策仍會相同。

能源成本透過合約逐步傳導至物價，速度慢於油價的每日調整。英國央行指出，企業避險與長期固定價格合約暫時吸收了成本，隨合約到期，成本影響將更普遍。Lombardelli表示，企業正以壓縮利潤率吸收成本，但承受能力有限。成品油溢價與運輸成本也仍偏高，中東煉油產能受損是壓力來源之一。

委員會迄今看到的第二輪效應證據不多，但希望防止能源成本改變工資及價格設定。即使在不含這類效應的溫和情境中，明年初通膨仍達4.8%；若衝突反覆升級，不利情境下CPI將於2027年第3季升至6.2%。另一個需求較弱的情境，則使通膨降至1.2%，也說明後續緊縮速度仍須視條件調整。

經濟成長也比原先假設強。央行將2026年成長預測由1.1%上修至1.6%，2027年由1.1%上修至1.3%，但將2028年由1.7%下修至1.2%。它認為升息前政策仍具限制性，卻較不確定既有緊縮能否及時讓通膨回到目標。央行估計，近期預算案將使明年第2季通膨降低0.25個百分點。通常較偏鴿派的Alan Taylor稱，此次支持升息是預防性措施；Dave Ramsden則強調，遏制第二輪效應的起始條件已較不利。

歐洲央行的討論仍未定案。克羅埃西亞籍管理委員會成員Ante Zigman認為，10月通膨加速後，12月再升息的可能性相當高，但鑑於近期油價大跌，不願將判斷延伸至2027年。總裁Christine Lagarde在米蘭表示，後續通膨與成長數據將決定12月是否需要緊縮。她強調，能源成本上升一方面推高價格，一方面抑制活動，科技與AI投資則支撐經濟韌性。工作人員將於12月提出新預測，目前存款利率維持2.5%。

瑞典的新數據，則對延長升息循環提出反證。10月排除能源的固定利率消費者物價指數（CPIF）初值年增率由0.5%放緩至0.1%，低於瑞典央行預估的0.6%與經濟學家中位數0.5%；整體CPIF由1.5%降至1.1%。這項數據在前一天升息之後公布，為後續政策評估提供了最新通膨資訊。

挪威維持存款利率4.5%，符合受訪16名分析師全數預期，並保留必要時升息的選項。總裁Ida Wolden Bache表示，通膨太高，利率可能還須維持高檔一段時間。企業工資成本持續支撐價格壓力，雖然薪資增速正在放緩。Oxford Economics的Rory Fennessy認為，能源價格若持續下降，可能使政策取向朝較中性立場移動；Handelsbanken的Marius Gonsholt Hov則強調國際利率預期與挪威克朗的影響。這次期中會議並未提出新的利率路徑。

捷克央行以4比3的些微差距，將基準利率調升25個基點至4%。總裁Ales Michl稱，這是微調政策限制程度，而非展開新循環，投資人因此下修進一步緊縮的預期。捷克克朗兌歐元一度貶值0.3%，走勢大致與區域貨幣一致。核心通膨已超過容忍區間上緣3%，服務、住宅、薪資成長與放款均屬國內風險；偏高的長期利率也已收緊金融條件。儘管理事會對本次行動的描述節制，遠期利率協議仍顯示未來一年約再升息兩次。

澳洲的新發展，是前次升息後的溝通爭議。副總裁Andrew Hauser否認10月談及通膨惡化，是試圖限制理事會的決策空間；他仍認為各項指標顯示通膨過高，並指出消費優於預期，同時為理事會內多元辯論辯護。Bloomberg訪問15名資深經濟學家及數名資金經理的調查顯示，市場預期現金利率升至4.85%後將暫停調整。貨幣市場對再升息機率的定價，以明年2月最高、為31%；2027年11月降息機率則由前一天35%升至76%。PIMCO的Adam Bowe預期，需求轉弱及限制性金融條件，最終將使央行能在2027年下半年降息。

## 亞洲融資環境與主權發債表現分化

印尼完成$30億美元計價伊斯蘭債券發行，優於預期的經濟成長數據，讓投資人在近期股市動盪之外，有了不同的評估依據。新債分3年、5年及10年期，最長天期殖利率為6.25%，初步討論約6.55%。這是MSCI警告可能將印尼股票自全球指數剔除以來，該國首度發行美元債；這項威脅先前已對印尼盾與本幣債造成壓力。

第3季GDP年增5.47%，高於經濟學家預估中位數5.2%，也高於第2季5.29%。政府消費增加近9%，投資增加6%，家庭支出與出口各增約5%。社會援助、燃料補貼及政府存放在國營銀行的現金支撐內需，大宗商品出口則協助連續錄得貿易順差。亞洲時段油價較低、美元較弱，提供支撐，印尼盾與債券在數據公布後保住稍早漲幅。

印尼仍面臨治理疑慮。Moody's與Fitch今年稍早已下調其主權評等展望；總統涉嫌遭竊聽的調查期間出現軍隊動員，政治緊張也升高。Barclays的Brian Tan認為，財政空間可繼續支撐成長，但MSCI檢討帶來的匯率壓力，可能迫使央行於2027年升息兩次。週四之前，印尼今年已透過各種幣別在海外募得近$130億，創下紀錄。此次伊斯蘭債發行完成融資，股票分類與國內政策風險仍待觀察。

印度債券在亞洲交易時段漲勢更強，先前油價下跌緩解通膨與進口支出的疑慮。指標殖利率一度下跌12個基點至7.07%，本週累計跌幅擴大至約35個基點。Karur Vysya Bank的VRC Reddy將預期政策利率高點由6.50%降至6.25%。盧比兌美元一度升值0.3%至94.3250，但ANZ的Dhiraj Nim預期，央行重建外匯存底將使盧比在93至94附近的升值受到限制。Barclays的Mitul Kotecha也指出，支撐匯率的措施可能包括收緊流動性管理。

日本標售則顯示，殖利率下降後需求有其限度。10年期公債投標倍數為3.21，低於前次3.76，也略低於過去12個月平均3.24；平均得標價與最低得標價差距由0.02擴大至0.25，期貨因而吐回部分漲幅。BNP Paribas Asset Management的Ryutaro Kimura表示，考量日本央行可能繼續升息，投資人認為2.7%區間低端的殖利率吸引力較小。指標殖利率已由9月底3.115%降至2.755%。隔夜指數交換顯示，12月前升息機率為79%，至1月升息25個基點則已完全反映在價格中。

菲律賓的通膨問題更為迫切。10月CPI年增率由7.2%加速至7.8%，高於經濟學家預估中位數7.6%，創2023年2月以來最高，主要由交通與住宅相關能源成本帶動。Barclays的Brian Tan上修通膨預估，並維持菲律賓央行12月再升息50個基點的預測，認為風險偏向更多緊縮。投資人預期央行持續應對，披索升值0.6%。下次政策會議為12月17日。

馬來西亞則維持隔夜利率2.75%，符合23名受訪經濟學家中17人的預期。央行警告，大宗商品、地緣政治與惡劣天候將推高2027年的整體及核心通膨，但預期成長仍具韌性。交換市場將六個月內升息機率由決策前25%上調至約32%。令吉保住稍早漲幅，約為兌美元4.05。燃料補貼與能源淨出口緩和了當前衝擊，9月通膨為1.8%，第3季成長率先行估值為5.3%。

中國國內融資利率方向相反。中國人民銀行將主要政策利率基準改為隔夜附買回利率後，最高評級銀行發行的1年期可轉讓定期存單，週三殖利率降至歷史低點1.39%。新的隔夜利率為1.25%，較原本7天期基準低15個基點；中國10年期公債殖利率降至約1.6%。國盛證券分析師Yang Yewei與Yi Yi解讀，實際融資基準已下移，因此預估年底至2027年初，存單殖利率將至1.30%至1.35%，10年期公債則至1.5%。

銀行融資成本下降之際，市場仍對個別地方發行人抱持戒心。先前報導的華發付款問題令投資人不安後，珠海大橫琴召開債權人會議。公司表示，為避免支付較高融資溢酬，已延後私募債發行，若市場情緒改善，可能本月稍晚重返市場。據熟悉其計畫的人士透露，若未發債，公司擬以現有現金償還11月23日到期的人民幣6億元債券。其2030年到期、票息2.08%的債券，殖利率自10月27日以來已上升200個基點。公司代表稱，對華發的曝險僅限合資房地產專案；大橫琴對這些專案提供逾人民幣20億元貸款，並為逾人民幣30億元融資提供擔保。

中國另宣布，計畫於11月9日當週在加拿大發行至多人民幣40億元綠色主權債，將人民幣債發行地點從香港、澳門與倫敦進一步擴展。OCBC的Frances Cheung認為，這可提升加拿大投資人對人民幣資產的認識。中國也另與銀行討論最快本月發行美元及離岸人民幣主權債的可能性，細節仍可能變動。

區域銀行財報帶來不同的信用疑慮。澳洲國民銀行（NAB）提列較高減損費用，並計畫最多裁減2,500人；星展（DBS）交易收入下降，執行長陳淑珊形容前景更加不確定。在貸款收入增加的效益充分顯現前，融資費用與信用損失準備升高，已先壓縮獲利。區域內各國成長及通膨路徑差異很大，這些財報則進一步呈現各銀行的營運狀況。

## 財政選擇與再融資成本拉開借款人差距

墨西哥以3比2表決降息25個基點至6.25%，出乎多數預料，受訪26名經濟學家中僅六人預期降息。墨西哥央行同時指引，利率應在新水準維持較長時間。披索起初跌至當日低點，隨後回升，墨西哥市午後稍早約為兌美元18.75。

理事會降息之際，也將年底整體通膨預測由3.5%上修至3.7%，核心通膨由3.6%上修至3.7%，仍預期2027年第4季回到3%目標。決策者承認第3季成長達3.2%，但認為經濟閒置仍將存在，活動風險也仍偏下行。近期整體物價雖上升，核心通膨降溫則支持降息。事先預料到這次行動的Barclays分析師Gabriel Casillas，仍預估2027年第1季再降息25個基點，與央行偏向長時間按兵不動的指引不同。

智利利率市場則在會議紀錄公布後，將預期緊縮時點提前。投資人幾乎確信三個月內將升息25個基點，一週前預期約為六個月內。3個月期交換利率一度上升8個基點，1年期上升4個基點。Scotiabank預期12月及2027年第1季各升息一次，使政策利率達5%。市場調整的重點是升息時點，最終利率高點預期維持不變；2年期交換利率週三已連跌五個交易日。UF遠期價格所反映的2月通膨高峰，從一週前5.7%降至5.5%，顯示油價下跌後，通膨定價下降與升息預期提前並存。T. Rowe Price的Christopher Mejia反對在投資復甦前升息，強調通膨由外部因素帶動、國內需求則疲弱。

阿根廷融資市場的失衡劇烈得多。披索隔夜附買回利率由前一天年化26%跳升至190%，創2025年10月期中選舉以來最高；美元債表現為新興市場最弱，部分債券價格下跌2美分。分析師將惡化情況與再融資壓力，以及政府可能在標售前買進披索債的猜測連結。

2029年與2030年到期債券，週三下午曾上漲逾4%，交易額超過披索3兆元，約為平常三倍，週四則恢復下跌。PPI、顧問公司1816及Buenos Aires Valores策略師Martín de la Fuente認為，交易的集中程度與規模顯示可能有官方買家。De la Fuente估計週三買進金額約披索2兆元；經濟部與央行均不予置評。PPI估計，下週標售對應的到期債務約披索10.5兆元，再接下來兩次標售對應的到期額合計另有披索66兆元；2027年強勢貨幣債務付款約$250億。Grit Capital的Belisario Álvarez de Toledo表示，利率波動顯示匯率穩定的優先程度高於利率穩定。

加拿大預算則明確選擇運用財政空間融資投資。總理Mark Carney政府預估，五年借款總額為加幣7,647億元，其中除了預算赤字，也包括主權財富基金等資本需求融資。本年度赤字預計加幣623億元，約占GDP的1.8%；淨債務預計占GDP的39.9%，低於春季估計的41.5%，未來五年則維持約40%。

計畫涵蓋電網、核電廠、採礦及林業等產業支出，以及住宅與減輕生活負擔的措施。自4月以來，五年期淨新增支出超過加幣1,500億元，其中包括已宣布、規模加幣360億元的投資扣抵措施。預算大致將額外收入投入支出。公共債務費用占收入比率，預計約五年內由約11%升至13.6%，因此這些投資能否帶來預期成長，更加重要。

Desjardins的Randall Bartlett質疑預測期內約加幣1,200億元新增收入，以及與未來負債折現相關、約加幣600億元成本減少的假設。財政部仍假設2030年10年期公債殖利率約3.7%。Bartlett認為，折現假設可能與整體財政預測所採用的假設不同；爭議在於支出與利息成本增加時，預估財政空間能維持多久。

貿易限制持續壓縮部分加拿大製造商。美國對廚房櫥櫃的關稅預定2027年1月1日由25%提高至50%。據Reuters報導，Cabico對美出貨量已較2024年低約25%，約700名員工中已裁減逾四分之一，並正考慮在美國建立生產合作關係。Muskoka Cabinet Company表示，70名員工約裁減40%，每週只營運三天。加拿大對部分進口櫥櫃徵收的25%臨時防衛措施最長持續200天，損害調查預計1月15日結束；業界要求關稅至少100%，目前仍屬提議。

南非財政比率改善的原因不同，來自國民所得帳修正。名目GDP上修5.3%，經濟規模由蘭特7.6兆元改為8兆元後，財政部將2025至2026年度債務高峰占GDP比率，由78.4%降至74.6%。2026至2027年度主要預算赤字占GDP比率由3.7%改為3.5%，初級盈餘則由1.7%改為1.6%。名目收入、支出與債務估值均未改變。分析師認為，比率改善可能有利信評；Oxford Economics的Jee-A van der Linde則強調，基期調整不會創造就業所需的實質成長，仍預估今年及明年成長約1%。

世界銀行新評估顯示，較貧窮主權借款人取得市場融資的成本仍高得多。開發中經濟體2025年外債創下$9.4兆紀錄；不含中國的中低所得國家淨債務流入接近$3,600億，主要由民間融資帶動。符合補助及優惠融資資格的較低所得國家，新民間貸款平均成本8.2%，新債券平均9.4%，處於1989年以來最高借款成本環境；經濟條件較強的開發中經濟體，新債平均成本則為5.5%。

世界銀行區分的是能否取得融資，以及是否負擔得起。許多新債只是買回舊債或分散還款時程，並未實質降低債務存量。該行也指出，阿根廷、哥倫比亞、安哥拉、奈及利亞與塞內加爾自2024年以來，愈來愈常運用總報酬交換，融資規模約$10億至$93億。這些安排迅速提供外幣，卻也帶來擔保品、再融資與透明度風險。世界銀行的重點在於民間融資恢復後的借款條件。

## 後續市場焦點

美東時間週五上午8時30分公布的10月就業報告，是檢視週四金融市場重新定價與當前經濟相符程度的下一項重大考驗。市場預估非農就業增加6.5萬人，前值2.9萬人；整體U-3失業率維持4.2%。民間就業預估增加6.4萬人，前值4.6萬人；製造業預估增加5,000人，前值9,000人。平均時薪預估月增0.3%，前值0.1%，年增率則由3%降至2.9%；平均每週工時預估維持34.4小時。招聘、薪資與工時的組合，能補足異常低的失業救濟申領數據所無法提供的細節。

美東時間上午10時接著公布11月密西根大學消費者信心初值，市場預估48，與10月相同。能源價格又經歷一週劇烈波動後，其中的通膨預期指標值得留意。John Williams、Alberto Musalem與Michelle Bowman預定週五公開露面，Lorie Logan則預定週四晚間發言。他們對通膨與需求的評估，可釐清市場降低緊縮預期的同時，決策者的判斷是否也在改變。

之後焦點轉向11月10日美東時間上午8時30分公布的10月CPI。市場預估整體物價月增0.3%，前值0.6%；核心物價月增0.2%，前值0.3%。這將檢驗單位勞動成本改善是否伴隨消費物價漲勢放慢。同一期間，美國財政部也將舉行已宣布的再融資標售：11月9日標售$580億3年期公債，11月10日標售$420億10年期公債，11月12日標售$250億30年期公債。此前漲勢由短端領軍，長端改善相對有限，標售將考驗需求。

能源外交仍是通膨與運輸的獨立風險。伊朗表示，週四又有三艘油輪受損，革命衛隊稱其中兩起由水雷造成，另一起為火災。英國海事貿易行動辦公室（UKMTO）另記錄，11月1日以來至少發生五起船舶事件，10月則有35起攻擊，為衝突以來單月最多。卡達持續斡旋，討論涵蓋荷姆茲海峽、美國封鎖伊朗港口、制裁及伊朗核計畫；一名伊朗官員表示，雙方仍有很大差距。市場期待外交進展，但事件持續發生，商船安全通行仍未解決。

AI融資眼前的問題，在於資料中心貸款組合與SpaceX租賃部位能以何種條件分銷，以及選後主管機關將如何處理個別開發案。這分別考驗次級市場流動性、新貸款人的參與及專案推進。Apple已完成融資，Meta歐元債首日表現也較強，顯示部分市場仍有籌資能力；但週四重新定價後，仰賴擴張的借款人能否取得資金、成本多高，仍未明朗。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended their rally as a steepening selloff in technology shares drove demand for safety and reduced expectations for further Federal Reserve tightening. The two-year yield fell 11.86 basis points to 4.4623%, outpacing a 5.32-basis-point decline in the 10-year to 4.8347%. Unlike the previous session's oil-led relief, Thursday's advance continued despite a rebound in crude, as concern about the financing and growth assumptions behind the artificial-intelligence buildout spread across equities and corporate debt.

The Nasdaq 100 lost 6.36% and semiconductor shares plunged 12.25%. CoreWeave bond yields exceeded 17%, while the cost of protecting SpaceX debt against default reached a record. U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably and hard-currency emerging-market spreads widened modestly. Yet the retreat was selective enough for Apple to raise $7.5 billion, with investors distinguishing its shareholder-return priorities from the much larger infrastructure demands confronting other technology borrowers.

Economic data and policymakers’ comments sent mixed signals. U.S. initial jobless claims fell below expectations to 189,000, while stronger productivity brought an unexpected decline in quarterly unit labor costs. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack continued to favor tighter policy, and Richmond's Tom Barkin supported gradual increases. Abroad, the Bank of England raised rates to 4% and warned of inflation approaching 5%, while Mexico surprised investors with a cut to 6.25%. The Treasury rally reflected a sharp adjustment in financial-market confidence alongside continuing, distinctly national inflation problems.

## Haven Demand Overtakes Oil and Labor Resilience

The Treasury session changed direction after the U.S. equity market opened. Yields had been rising as oil recovered from its recent lows, but the deepening technology retreat brought buyers into government debt. Capital Group fixed-income investment director Anmol Sinha linked the move to concern that falling chip stocks signaled a slower pace of capital expenditure. The concern extended beyond the immediate demand for havens: less investment in AI infrastructure could also reduce the growth and policy-rate outlook that had helped push yields higher earlier in the autumn.

Shorter maturities led the closing advance. The five-year yield fell 8.14 basis points to 4.6045%, while the 30-year declined just 2.23 basis points to 5.2539%. The two- to 10-year curve steepened 6.54 basis points to 37.24 basis points, and the two- to 30-year gap widened 9.63 basis points to 79.16 basis points. The front-end concentration pointed to a stronger role for changing policy expectations.

Real yields accounted for most of the 10-year move. The corresponding TIPS yield fell 4.17 basis points to 2.5977%, while 10-year inflation compensation declined 1.15 basis points to 2.237%. Over the week, the balance remained different: the nominal yield was 10.22 basis points lower, with the breakeven down 11.28 basis points and the real yield up 1.06 basis points. Thursday therefore added a meaningful real-yield decline to a weekly recovery still dominated by lower inflation compensation. Over the month, the 10-year yield had fallen 47.21 basis points, including a 34.63-basis-point retreat in its real component.

Interest-rate derivatives reflected the change in sentiment without abandoning the prospect of another increase. Bloomberg's intraday account said traders still leaned toward a quarter-point Fed hike on December 9, but short-rate options included trades targeting no move, and wagers on further tightening next year were reduced. Treasury options also drew demand for additional gains. One trade targeted a 10-year yield of 4.7% by the end of next week and another, expiring November 20, around 4.35%. Those were option positions expressing possible outcomes, rather than an agreed market forecast.

The equity losses were both large and concentrated in the investment theme unsettling creditors. The S&P 500 fell 4.36% to 7,353.73 and the Nasdaq 100 finished at 26,629.81. The VIX jumped 69.66% to 28.18. Underwhelming outlooks from Qualcomm and Arm added company-specific pressure to fears of tougher data-center regulation after Democratic gains in the midterm elections. The semiconductor index's daily fall left it down 21.77% over the week and 31.59% over the month.

Treasuries drew haven demand even as oil rebounded. Brent futures rose 4.89% to $99.25 a barrel and WTI gained 3.50% to $91.20, although both remained more than 10% below their week-earlier levels. Gold futures rose 0.61% to $4,097.90 an ounce, while the Dollar Index edged up 0.07% to 101.584. Investors moved away from growth-sensitive assets as oil recovered from its recent decline.

Fresh U.S. labor figures gave little indication of accelerating dismissals. Initial unemployment claims fell 6,000 to 189,000 in the week ended October 31, below the 196,000 consensus. The previous week was revised to 195,000 from 194,000. The four-week average fell 2,250 to 194,750, and Reuters described the headline as matching July's low, the lowest since 1969.

Continuing claims were less favorable. They increased 23,000 to 1.718 million for the week ended October 24, above the 1.710 million consensus, after a downward revision of the previous reading to 1.695 million. The insured unemployment rate held at 1.1%. Low entry into unemployment thus coexisted with a modest increase in the number continuing to receive benefits. Challenger's separate October tally of announced job cuts was 43,994, compared with 43,281 previously and a 51,000 forecast.

Productivity offered a more direct improvement in measured inflation costs. Preliminary Q3 nonfarm business productivity increased at a 3.6% seasonally adjusted annual rate, exceeding the 2.8% consensus. Output grew 3.7% while hours increased just 0.1%. With hourly compensation up 2.9%, unit labor costs fell 0.7%, rather than rising the expected 0.6%. Productivity was 2.1% higher than a year earlier, although unit labor costs still increased 2.4% over that period.

The improvement was not uniform across production. Manufacturing productivity rose only 0.3% annualized, with output up 1.3% and hours up 1%. Durable-goods productivity increased 2.2%, but nondurable productivity fell 1.7%. Manufacturing unit labor costs rose 2.7% annualized and 4% year on year. The aggregate decline in labor cost per unit of output therefore sat alongside continuing pressure in factories.

Revisions also changed the comparison. Q2 nonfarm business productivity growth was revised up 0.7 percentage point to 2.1%, and unit labor cost growth was raised by the same amount to 1.9%. Annual average productivity growth for 2025 and 2024 became 2.3% and 3.2%, respectively, both 0.2 percentage point higher than previously estimated. Since Q4 2019, productivity had grown at a 2.2% annualized rate, versus 1.5% in the preceding business cycle. The labor share of output reached 53%, its lowest reading in the series beginning in 1947.

Hammack's policy assessment remained restrictive. Speaking in Zurich, the Cleveland Fed president said policy needed to move to a restrictive stance to restore inflation to 2% in a timely manner, and favored more frequent, smaller adjustments when possible to reduce the risk of falling behind. She had been one of two dissenters against last week's decision to hold rates. She described price pressure as broad-based, arising from both supply and demand, and saw modest signs that a labor market long characterized by low hiring and low firing might be strengthening.

Barkin, speaking separately, reiterated support for gradual rate increases but declined to specify how far rates should rise. The market's response to an equity-led growth risk was consequently running ahead of any comparable shift in those officials' stated preferences.

FHN Financial's Will Compernolle cautioned that a reversal in AI investment might initially have only a limited employment effect because the boom had been capital-intensive and added relatively few jobs. Any wider financial spillover into the economy would take longer to appear. That assessment helps explain why Thursday's financial-market repricing could be substantial even with weekly claims still unusually low.

## AI Credit Reprices While Apple Secures Funding

The sharpest corporate-credit deterioration came among borrowers closely tied to the AI construction cycle. CoreWeave's bond yield above 17% marked a further worsening from the previous session, while SpaceX's default-protection cost reached its highest level and increased much more than those of other hyperscalers. Investors were reassessing exposure to permitting delays, political scrutiny and funding demands as the technology-equity selloff broadened.

The distinctions within the sector remained important. Bloomberg reported only marginal increases in the cost of protecting other hyperscalers' debt. Its credit analyst Robert Schiffman argued that tighter permitting, grid-cost rules and local opposition could support the credit of large technology customers if slower construction curtailed capital intensity and external funding needs. Developers dependent on rapid expansion faced a less comfortable adjustment. Intrepid Capital Management's Hunter Hayes warned that some creditors were relying on the next lender to provide repayment funding and that weaker market access could leave companies unable to complete their plans.

SpaceX's financing illustrated the size and complexity of that exposure. Goldman Sachs and Apollo were in talks with investors about distributing parts of a roughly $40 billion equipment-finance lease signed last week to fund chips. Prospective buyers were being asked about slices of as much as $500 million before formal syndication, according to people familiar with the discussions. The arrangement was structured to keep the debt off SpaceX's balance sheet. Distribution talks remained underway as the market price of its credit protection rose.

A separate sale process involved about $500 million of data-center loans, including a $25 million piece backing a New Mexico site within the Stargate project involving OpenAI, SoftBank and Oracle. RBC Global Asset Management's Andrzej Skiba said hedge funds had been heavy sellers of AI-linked debt over recent weeks, with leveraged positions being unwound. He also identified selling in media and telecommunications debt.

Project news added specific uncertainties to the broader political concerns. Microsoft's decision not to extend a contract at an Nscale data center in Texas, reported by a person familiar with the matter, came ahead of the startup's planned public offering. Oracle's proposed $165 billion New Mexico complex faced a potential further delay after its power developer agreed to give regulators more time to review an air permit. Micron suspended plans for a memory-chip plant in Taiwan amid a protracted labor dispute, according to people familiar with the matter. Those developments involved different contractual, regulatory and operating issues, each bearing on the timing of infrastructure delivery.

Apple's completed financing showed investors continuing to differentiate among technology business models. Its seven-part $7.5 billion offering attracted about $31 billion of peak orders, more than four times the amount sold, despite the broader market retreat. Maturities ranged from two to 10 years. The longest bonds, due in 2036, priced at 55 basis points over Treasuries after tightening 25 basis points during marketing.

That premium compared with 65 basis points for recently issued Microsoft debt of similar maturity, 160 basis points for Meta and 310 basis points for Oracle. Apple, rated AA+ by S&P Global Ratings, intended to use proceeds for general corporate purposes, including share repurchases. Schiffman characterized its return as more opportunistic than funding-driven, with shareholder distributions remaining a greater capital priority than the infrastructure spending confronting its peers. Bank of America, Deutsche Bank, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan managed the transaction.

Europe provided another measure of selective demand. All six tranches of Meta's newly issued €9 billion deal were indicated above par on their first trading day, including bid quotations, after pricing just below face value. The latest account put the final order book at €62 billion, above the €53 billion previously reported. Alphabet's euro bonds sold Monday were also indicated above par. These secondary-market gains followed substantial new-issue compensation; they coexisted with much weaker pricing among highly leveraged AI borrowers.

Broader credit returns reflected the competing effects of lower Treasury yields and weaker risk appetite. LQD returned about 0.15%, including distributions, while HYG lost 0.31% and JNK fell 0.27%. EMB declined 0.52%. The clear widening in U.S. high-yield spreads and modest widening in hard-currency emerging-market spreads contrasted with the strong advance in government debt.

Outside technology, Volkswagen paid heavily for hybrid funding but attracted large orders. Its €1.95 billion green offering comprised two subordinated bonds yielding 7.1% and 7.45%, about 250 basis points above its outstanding senior debt. Bloomberg compared that gap with roughly 67 basis points between senior and subordinated debt in European ICE indexes. Each tranche drew orders exceeding eight times the amount offered.

The proceeds will partially refinance hybrids callable in 2027. The new coupons are 6.875% and 7.25%, compared with 3.875% and 3.748% on the outstanding securities. The higher cost accompanies pressure from weaker Chinese demand, tariffs and competition, after VW reported a €5.86 billion Q3 operating loss driven by writedowns and restructuring charges. Hybrid debt carries partial equity treatment from rating firms, giving the company a balance-sheet reason to retain the instrument even at a considerable premium to senior borrowing. Edmond de Rothschild portfolio manager Marc Lacraz cited VW's cash position and compared yields above 7% with about 5.5% for the euro BB index.

The acquisition-financing pipeline also continued to develop. Goldman Sachs, Bank of America and Barclays were selected to lead a $3.1 billion package for CD&R and McKesson's purchase of Option Care Health, according to people familiar with the matter. It is expected to combine leveraged loans with secured and unsecured bonds. Sale timing was still being finalized, with the acquisition due to close in the first half of 2027. The approximately $5.8 billion enterprise-value transaction would leave CD&R with 51% and McKesson with 49%, following about $1.4 billion of investment by the latter. This prospective supply follows October U.S. junk-bond sales of $14.6 billion, down 18% from a year earlier, and leveraged-loan sales down more than 10%.

Bank of America separately combined its credit-macro, fixed-income ETF and high-grade trading operations into a single platform led by Rory O'Donovan and Amit Patel, alongside their existing responsibilities. The consolidation comes as Crisil Coalition Greenwich puts average daily U.S. high-grade and junk-bond trading at a record $61.6 billion through October, versus $55.2 billion in 2025. Electronic trading accounted for 46% of U.S. high-grade activity, up from 44% last year and 30% in 2021. The bank said the structure would integrate liquidity provision across instruments used to trade and hedge credit risk.

## Britain's Hike Exposes Uneven Inflation Risks

The Bank of England raised its policy rate 25 basis points to 4%, its first increase since 2023, with every policymaker favoring tighter policy. Eight backed the quarter-point move; Catherine Mann wanted 50 basis points. The distinction matters to the breadth of the decision: there was no vote to leave rates unchanged, even though the chosen increment passed 8-1.

Governor Andrew Bailey saw a case for a further increase followed by a more conditional approach. Without progress toward resolving the Iran conflict or other news reducing inflation pressure, another move could be warranted. He also rejected the idea that Thursday necessarily began a long sequence of increases. Traders moved to price around a 50% probability of a December hike after the announcement and almost three further quarter-point increases by the end of next year. Two-year gilt yields rose about 3 basis points to 4.77% in Bloomberg's decision account, while its broader market summary put the 10-year little changed at 5.13%.

The new inflation forecasts showed the scale of the price pressures facing Britain. CPI was projected to peak at 4.9% in Q2 2027, compared with the 3.2% peak envisaged in July. Household energy bills are forecast to rise about 25% when the regulated cap resets in January. The forecast's market-price assumptions, using the 15 days through October 27, incorporated Brent 38% above the July projection and natural gas 81% higher. Bailey said the decision would have been the same even had the committee known the energy-price developments of the previous 48 hours.

Transmission through contracts makes the inflation path slower than the oil market's daily adjustment. The BOE said businesses' hedges and long-term fixed-price agreements had temporarily absorbed costs that would become more widespread as those contracts expired. Lombardelli said companies were trying to contain costs through margins but had limits to that capacity. Refined-product premiums and shipping costs also remained elevated, with damaged Middle Eastern refining capacity contributing to the pressure.

The committee had seen little evidence of second-round effects so far, but wanted to prevent energy costs from changing wage and price setting. Even its mild scenario, without such effects, showed inflation reaching 4.8% early next year. Repeated escalation in the conflict would lift CPI to 6.2% in Q3 2027 in the adverse scenario. A weaker-demand alternative instead had inflation falling to 1.2%, illustrating why the pace of subsequent tightening remained conditional.

Growth had also been stronger than assumed. The BOE raised its 2026 forecast to 1.6% from 1.1% and its 2027 projection to 1.3% from 1.1%, while cutting 2028 to 1.2% from 1.7%. It judged policy still restrictive before the increase but was less confident that existing restraint would return inflation to target promptly. The bank estimated the recent budget would reduce inflation by 0.25 percentage point in Q2 next year. Alan Taylor, usually among the more dovish members, described his support as an insurance increase; Dave Ramsden emphasized less favorable starting conditions for containing second-round effects.

The ECB debate remained open. Croatian Governing Council member Ante Zigman saw a substantial chance of another increase in December after October inflation accelerated, but declined to extend that judgment into 2027 given the sharp recent fall in oil. President Christine Lagarde, speaking in Milan, said incoming inflation and growth data would determine whether December tightening was necessary. She emphasized that higher energy costs both raised prices and restrained activity, while technology and AI investment supported resilience. Updated staff forecasts arrive in December. The deposit rate remains 2.5%.

Sweden supplied fresh counterevidence to the case for an extended hiking cycle. Preliminary October CPIF excluding energy slowed to 0.1% annually from 0.5%, below both the Riksbank's 0.6% estimate and economists' 0.5% median. Headline CPIF fell to 1.1% from 1.5%. The release followed the previous day's rate increase and provided updated inflation data for future policy assessments.

Norway held its deposit rate at 4.5%, as all 16 surveyed analysts expected, and retained the option to increase it if necessary. Governor Ida Wolden Bache said inflation was too high and rates would likely need to remain elevated for some time. Corporate wage costs continued to support price pressure, although wage growth was moderating. Oxford Economics' Rory Fennessy said sustained energy declines could move the balance toward a more neutral stance; Handelsbanken's Marius Gonsholt Hov emphasized the role of international rate expectations and the krone. The interim meeting brought no new rate path.

The Czech National Bank raised its benchmark 25 basis points to 4% in a narrow 4-3 vote. Governor Ales Michl called the increase a fine-tuning of restraint rather than the start of a new cycle, and investors trimmed expectations for further tightening. The koruna weakened as much as 0.3% against the euro, broadly alongside regional currencies. Core inflation had exceeded the 3% upper edge of the tolerance range, with services, housing, wage growth and lending among domestic risks. Elevated longer-term rates were already tightening financial conditions. Forward agreements still suggested roughly two further increases over the next year, despite the board's restrained description of its latest action.

Australia's new development was a dispute about communication after its earlier increase, not another policy decision. Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser denied trying to constrain the board through his October comments on deteriorating inflation. He maintained that inflation was too high across measures and pointed to better-than-expected consumption, while defending the board's diverse debate. A Bloomberg survey of 15 senior economists and several money managers found expectations of a pause after the cash rate reached 4.85%. Money markets put the highest probability of another increase at 31% for February and priced a 76% chance of a cut in November 2027, up from 35% a day earlier. PIMCO's Adam Bowe expected weaker demand and restrictive conditions eventually to permit easing in the second half of 2027.

## Asian Funding and Sovereign Access Diverge

Indonesia completed a $3 billion dollar sukuk sale as a stronger-than-expected growth release gave investors a different assessment from the recent equity-market turmoil. The offering spanned three, five and 10 years, with the longest maturity yielding 6.25%, against initial discussions around 6.55%. It was the country's first dollar issuance since MSCI warned that its equities could be removed from global indexes, a threat that had pressured the rupiah and local bonds.

Q3 GDP rose 5.47% from a year earlier, exceeding the 5.2% economist median and Q2's 5.29%. Government consumption increased nearly 9%, investment grew 6%, and household spending and exports each rose about 5%. Social assistance, fuel subsidies and government cash placed with state banks supported domestic demand, while commodity exports helped deliver successive trade surpluses. The rupiah and bonds retained earlier gains after the release, supported by cheaper oil and a softer dollar during the Asian session.

Indonesia continued to face governance concerns: Moody's and Fitch had lowered their sovereign outlooks earlier this year, and political tension increased after troops were mobilized amid an investigation into alleged presidential wiretapping. Barclays' Brian Tan saw further growth support from fiscal room but expected currency pressure surrounding MSCI's review could require two rate increases in 2027. Before Thursday, Indonesia had already sold nearly $13 billion overseas this year across currencies, a record. The new sukuk provided funding as risks to equity classification and domestic policy remained under scrutiny.

India's bonds rallied more sharply in Asian trading as the earlier oil decline eased concerns over inflation and the import bill. Benchmark yields fell as much as 12 basis points to 7.07%, extending the weekly decline to about 35 basis points. Karur Vysya Bank's VRC Reddy lowered his expected policy-rate peak to 6.25% from 6.50%. The rupee strengthened as much as 0.3% to 94.3250 per dollar, although ANZ's Dhiraj Nim expected central-bank reserve rebuilding to limit gains around 93-94. Barclays' Mitul Kotecha also identified the possibility of tighter liquidity management among measures to support the currency.

Japan's auction showed the limits to demand after a fall in yields. The 10-year sale's bid-to-cover ratio was 3.21, below the previous 3.76 and slightly below the 12-month average of 3.24. The gap between the average and lowest accepted prices widened to 0.25 from 0.02, and futures surrendered some gains. BNP Paribas Asset Management's Ryutaro Kimura said investors found yields in the low 2.7% range less attractive given the prospect of further BOJ increases. The benchmark yield had declined to 2.755% from 3.115% in late September. Overnight-indexed swaps indicated a 79% probability of an increase by December, with a quarter-point move fully priced by January.

The Philippines reported a more urgent inflation problem. October CPI accelerated to 7.8% from 7.2%, exceeding the 7.6% economist median and reaching its highest rate since February 2023. Transport and housing-related energy costs drove the acceleration. Barclays' Brian Tan retained a forecast for another 50-basis-point BSP increase in December, with risks toward more tightening, while raising his inflation estimates. The peso rose 0.6% as investors anticipated a continued response. The next policy meeting is December 17.

Malaysia instead held its overnight rate at 2.75%, as 17 of 23 surveyed economists expected. The central bank warned that commodities, geopolitical developments and adverse weather would lift headline and core inflation in 2027, but expected growth to remain resilient. Swaps increased the probability of a hike within six months to about 32% from 25% before the decision. The ringgit retained earlier gains at about 4.05 per dollar. Fuel subsidies and net energy exports have moderated the immediate shock, with September inflation at 1.8% and advance Q3 growth at 5.3%.

China's domestic funding rates moved in the opposite direction. One-year negotiable certificates of deposit issued by top-rated banks yielded a record-low 1.39% on Wednesday after the PBOC shifted its principal policy anchor to overnight repos. The new overnight rate of 1.25% was 15 basis points below the former seven-day benchmark. China's 10-year sovereign yield fell to around 1.6%. Guosheng Securities analysts Yang Yewei and Yi Yi forecast NCD yields at 1.30%-1.35% and the 10-year at 1.5% around year-end and early 2027, reflecting their interpretation of the lower effective funding anchor.

Bank funding costs fell as investors remained cautious about individual local issuers. Zhuhai Da Heng Qin held creditor meetings after Huafa's previously reported payment problems unsettled investors. It said it had delayed a private bond sale to avoid paying a premium and could return later this month if sentiment improved. Otherwise, people familiar with its plans said it intended to repay a 600 million yuan bond due November 23 using cash on hand. The yield on its 2.08% bond due in 2030 had risen 200 basis points since October 27. A representative described exposure to Huafa as confined to joint-venture property projects, to which Da Heng Qin had lent more than 2 billion yuan and guaranteed over 3 billion yuan of financing.

China also announced plans to sell up to 4 billion yuan of green sovereign bonds in Canada during the week of November 9, extending its yuan issuance venues beyond Hong Kong, Macau and London. OCBC's Frances Cheung said the sale could broaden awareness of yuan assets among Canadian investors. Separate discussions with banks concerned possible dollar and offshore-yuan sovereign offerings as early as this month, with details still subject to change.

Regional bank earnings brought a different credit concern. NAB reported higher impairment charges and plans to cut up to 2,500 jobs, while DBS suffered a decline in trading income and Chief Executive Tan Su Shan described a more uncertain outlook. Higher funding expenses and credit-loss provisions were pressuring profitability before the full benefit of higher lending income arrived. Those operating results added bank-specific information to a region otherwise displaying widely differing sovereign growth and inflation paths.

## Fiscal Choices and Refinancing Costs Separate Borrowers

Mexico cut its policy rate 25 basis points to 6.25% in a 3-2 vote, surprising a survey in which only six of 26 economists expected easing. Banxico paired the reduction with guidance that rates should remain at the new level for an extended period. The peso initially fell to a session low before recovering, trading around 18.75 per dollar in the early afternoon in Mexico City.

The board reduced rates while raising its year-end headline inflation projection to 3.7% from 3.5% and its core forecast to 3.7% from 3.6%. It still expected convergence to the 3% target in Q4 2027. Policymakers acknowledged Q3 growth of 3.2% but said slack would persist and risks to activity remained downward. Cooling core inflation provided support for the decision despite the recent rise in headline prices. Barclays' Gabriel Casillas, who had anticipated the cut, continued to forecast another quarter-point reduction in Q1 2027, while the board's own guidance favored a prolonged hold.

Chile's rates market instead brought forward expected tightening after newly published minutes. Investors moved toward a near-certain quarter-point increase within three months, rather than roughly six months a week earlier. Three-month swaps rose as much as 8 basis points and one-year rates 4 basis points. Scotiabank expected increases in December and Q1 2027 to bring the policy rate to 5%. The market adjustment concerned timing more than the eventual peak, with two-year swaps having fallen for a fifth session on Wednesday. UF forwards lowered the expected February inflation peak to 5.5% from 5.7% a week earlier, showing that earlier tightening expectations coexisted with reduced inflation pricing after oil's decline. T. Rowe Price's Christopher Mejia opposed raising rates before a recovery in investment, emphasizing externally driven inflation and weak domestic demand.

Argentina faced a much sharper funding dislocation. The overnight peso repo rate jumped to an annualized 190% from 26% a day earlier, its highest since the October 2025 midterms. Dollar bonds were the weakest in emerging markets, with some issues losing 2 cents. Analysts linked the deterioration to refinancing pressures and speculation about government purchases of peso bonds ahead of auctions.

Notes due in 2029 and 2030 had rallied more than 4% Wednesday afternoon as trading exceeded 3 trillion pesos, roughly triple the usual volume, before resuming their decline Thursday. PPI, consultancy 1816 and Buenos Aires Valores strategist Martín de la Fuente said the concentration and size suggested an official buyer. De la Fuente estimated Wednesday purchases around 2 trillion pesos. The Economy Ministry and central bank declined to comment. PPI put maturities at about 10.5 trillion pesos for next week's auction and another 66 trillion pesos across the following two sales; hard-currency debt payments total roughly $25 billion in 2027. Grit Capital's Belisario Álvarez de Toledo said the rate volatility suggested exchange-rate stability was taking priority over interest-rate stability.

Canada's budget set out a deliberate use of fiscal capacity to finance investment. Prime Minister Mark Carney's government projected C$764.7 billion of borrowing over five years, including financing beyond the budget deficit for capital requirements such as the sovereign wealth fund. The current-year deficit was forecast at C$62.3 billion, or about 1.8% of GDP. Net debt was projected at 39.9% of GDP, below the spring estimate of 41.5%, and near 40% over the next five years.

The program includes industrial spending on electricity networks, nuclear plants, mining and forestry, along with housing and affordability measures. Net new spending since April exceeded C$150 billion over five years, including the already announced C$36 billion investment deduction. The budget largely committed the revenue windfall to spending. Public debt charges were projected to rise from about 11% of revenue to 13.6% in roughly five years, placing greater weight on whether the investment generates the intended growth.

Desjardins' Randall Bartlett questioned the assumptions behind approximately C$120 billion of additional revenue over the projection period and about C$60 billion of cost reductions associated with discounting future liabilities. The Finance Department retained an assumption of roughly 3.7% for the 10-year government yield in 2030. Bartlett suggested the discounting assumptions might differ from those used in the wider fiscal forecasts. The dispute concerns the durability of projected fiscal room as spending and interest costs rise.

Trade restrictions continued to constrain some Canadian manufacturers. U.S. tariffs on kitchen cabinets are scheduled to rise from 25% to 50% on January 1, 2027. Reuters reported that Cabico's U.S. shipment volumes were already about 25% below 2024 levels and that it had cut more than a quarter of its approximately 700 employees. The company was considering production partnerships in the U.S. Muskoka Cabinet Company reported cutting about 40% of its 70-person workforce and operating three days a week. Canada's provisional 25% safeguard on some imported cabinets lasts up to 200 days, with an injury investigation due to conclude January 15. Industry demands for a duty of at least 100% remain proposals.

South Africa's improved fiscal ratios came from a different source: revised national accounts. Treasury lowered the estimated 2025-26 debt peak to 74.6% of GDP from 78.4%, after nominal GDP was revised 5.3% higher. The revised economy totaled 8 trillion rand rather than 7.6 trillion. The 2026-27 main budget deficit became 3.5% of GDP instead of 3.7%, while the primary surplus was 1.6% rather than 1.7%. Treasury left nominal revenue, spending and debt estimates unchanged. Analysts saw possible rating benefits from better ratios; Oxford Economics' Jee-A van der Linde emphasized that the rebasing did not create the real growth needed for employment and still forecast expansion around 1% this year and next.

A new World Bank assessment showed how much more expensive market access remained for poorer sovereigns. External debt of developing economies reached a record $9.4 trillion in 2025. Net debt inflows to low- and middle-income countries excluding China approached $360 billion, driven substantially by private financing. Among lower-income countries eligible for grants and concessional financing, new private loans cost an average 8.2% and new bonds 9.4%, the highest borrowing-cost environment since 1989. New bonds for developing economies with stronger economic conditions averaged 5.5%.

The bank's distinction was between obtaining financing and affording it. Many new issues bought back old debt or spread repayments over time without materially reducing debt stocks. It also identified growing use since 2024 of total-return swaps in Argentina, Colombia, Angola, Nigeria and Senegal, with financing amounts around $1 billion-$9.3 billion. Such arrangements supplied foreign currency quickly while introducing collateral, refinancing and transparency risks. The finding concerned the terms of renewed private lending.

## Forward Market Significance

Friday's October employment report, due at 8:30 a.m. Eastern, is the next major test of how much Thursday's financial repricing corresponds to the current economy. Consensus calls for 65,000 additional payrolls after 29,000, with headline U-3 unemployment unchanged at 4.2%. Private payrolls are expected to increase 64,000 after 46,000, and manufacturing employment 5,000 after 9,000. Average hourly earnings are expected to rise 0.3% monthly after 0.1%, with annual growth easing to 2.9% from 3%. Average weekly hours are expected to hold at 34.4. The hiring, wage and hours combination will add detail that unusually low claims alone cannot provide.

November's preliminary Michigan sentiment reading follows at 10 a.m. Eastern, with consensus at 48, unchanged from October. Its inflation-expectations measures will be relevant after another week of volatile energy prices. John Williams, Alberto Musalem and Michelle Bowman have scheduled Friday appearances, while Lorie Logan is scheduled to speak Thursday evening. Their assessments can clarify whether the reduction in market expectations for tightening is accompanied by a change in policymakers' judgment of inflation and demand.

The calendar then moves to October CPI on November 10 at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. Consensus expects headline prices to rise 0.3% monthly after 0.6%, and core prices 0.2% after 0.3%. That release will test whether the improved unit-labor-cost figures are accompanied by slower consumer-price increases. Treasury's announced refunding auctions fall in the same period: $58 billion of three-year notes on November 9, $42 billion of 10-year notes on November 10 and $25 billion of 30-year bonds on November 12. Demand will be tested after a front-end-led rally that left the long end relatively less improved.

Energy diplomacy remains an independent risk to both inflation and transport. Iran said three more tankers were damaged Thursday, with the Revolutionary Guards attributing two incidents to mines and another to fire. UKMTO separately recorded at least five vessel incidents since November 1 and 35 attacks in October, the conflict's highest monthly count. Qatar continued mediating discussions covering Hormuz, the U.S. blockade of Iranian ports, sanctions and Iran's nuclear program; an Iranian official said the sides remained far apart. The continued incidents leave safe commercial passage unresolved even as markets anticipate diplomatic progress.

For AI financing, the immediate questions are the terms on which the data-center loan portfolio and SpaceX lease exposure can be distributed, and how authorities will treat individual developments after the elections. These are distinct tests of secondary liquidity, new lender participation and project execution. Apple's completed transaction and Meta's firmer euro debut show continued funding capacity in parts of the market, while Thursday's repricing leaves the cost and availability of capital for expansion-dependent borrowers unsettled.

overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries extended their rally after the technology selloff deepened, raising concerns about AI capital spending and its contribution to growth. The 2-year yield fell 11.86 basis points to 4.4623%, versus a 5.32-basis-point decline in the 10-year to 4.8347%, steepening the curve. Most of the 10-year decline came from a 4.17-basis-point fall in real yields; inflation compensation fell 1.15 basis points. That differed from the week's advance, which remained dominated by lower inflation compensation.

The Nasdaq 100 lost 6.36% and semiconductor shares fell 12.25%. CoreWeave bond yields exceeded 17% and SpaceX default-protection costs reached a record. U.S. high-yield spreads widened noticeably and hard-currency EM spreads widened modestly, but Apple completed a $7.5 billion bond sale with about $31 billion of peak orders, demonstrating continued differentiation among technology borrowers.

Treasuries drew haven demand even as oil rebounded. Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000, while stronger Q3 productivity helped unit labor costs decline 0.7% annualized. Hammack continued to favor tighter Fed policy and Barkin supported gradual increases. Abroad, the BOE raised rates to 4% as it projected inflation approaching 5%, whereas Mexico unexpectedly cut to 6.25%. Friday's employment report is the nearest test of whether the financial repricing corresponds to weaker economic conditions.
